text:
### Observed differences

- Two blocks of activities exchanged their place in the case. In the earlier window, A14, A18, A21, A22 and A23 each sat at about one third into the trace (mean relative positions about 0.32–0.33), while A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 sat at about 0.62–0.63; in the later window, the first block sits at about 0.68–0.71 and the second at about 0.38–0.39. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- All measured order relations between the two blocks reversed. Before, A14 preceded A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 whenever both occurred (about 21 in 100 traces, never the reverse); in the later window these activities precede A14 in about 17 in 100 traces, again never the reverse; the same reversal shows for A18, A21, A22 and A23 against the other block. [REL001, REL003, REL005, REL008, REL009, REL014, REL020, REL026, REL030, REL040, REL044]
- Against the two connectors the reversal is complete: before, A24 and A28 came before A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window, each of these five comes before A24 and A28 in 100 in 100 traces. [REL012, REL013, REL018, REL019, REL024, REL025, REL033, REL034, REL038, REL039]
- Successors changed hands consistently. Before, A14, A18, A21, A22 and A23 were always followed by A24; in the later window they are always followed by A29. Before, A15–A20 passed on to A29 in roughly 14–27 out of 100 of their outgoing transitions; in the later window they pass to A24 in roughly 17–25 out of 100, and A29 is no longer observed after them. A28 now leads to A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 instead of A15–A20, and A39 leads to A15–A20 instead of the first block. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]
- Participation hardly moved: A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 appear in every trace in both windows; each of A14, A18, A21, A22, A23 appears in about 16–23 in 100 traces in both windows, with the five shares summing to about 100 in 100, consistent with exactly one of them per case. A24 and A28 also remain in every trace, between the two blocks, shifting somewhat later (A24 mean position about 0.36 to 0.48; A28 about 0.54 to 0.66). [POS001, POS002, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012, REL008, REL012]
- Screening context: 69 control-flow items qualified against about 0.65 expected if nothing had changed (131 units tested), far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [screening]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two blocks of activities exchanged their order in the process. Before, a case ran one of A14, A18, A21, A22, A23 early (about one third in), followed by A24, then A28, then the block A15, A16, A17, A19, A20 late, which passed on to A29; in the later window, A15–A20 run early and pass to A24 and then A28, while one of A14, A18, A21, A22, A23 runs late and passes to A29. Participation of every involved activity stayed essentially the same, so this is a change in ordering, not in which activities run. [REL012, REL013, DIR001, DIR002, DIR011, DIR012, POS001, POS002]

The signs are direct and consistent: the relational items show the order reversals without exception (including complete reversals against A24 and A28), the two groups' positions move in opposite directions, which a change in trace length alone could not produce, and the successor handovers flip in the same direction throughout. The number of qualifying items (69 against about 0.65 expected) cannot be explained by chance as a whole, although the items largely describe one underlying exchange rather than independent changes. [REL012, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, screening]

Limitations: positions are event positions rather than clock times; the positions of A29 and A39 are not measured, so their roles are inferred only from successor patterns; and the evidence cannot fully rule out that the two windows sampled two different, internally fixed variant populations rather than a reordering within one process, although the single, flipped order observed in each window fits the exchange reading. [REL001, DIR001, POS001]

Other differences: within the A15–A20 block, internal transition shares shifted modestly, by up to about 10 percentage points (for example A15 to A17 rose from about 14 to about 24 out of 100 of A15's outgoing transitions), alongside the exit change from A29 to A24. [DIR002]
